summary: Small Deschutes NF hill used as a secondary lookout point from 1915, with a telephone spur line; a temporary post on the hill in 1924 and an intermediate lookout in 1927.

events.note: Spur telephone line built about a third of a mile from the Crane Prairie line to the summit; the hill was used as a secondary lookout point. First call came over the line on July 7.
William Beaton was transferred permanently to Paulina Peak from his temporary post on Bates Butte.
An intermediate lookout was stationed at Bates Butte due to extreme fire danger (August 1927).

evidence.supports: 1915 spur telephone line to the summit; secondary lookout point; near Big River Station
evidence.quote: Ranger Oney has constructed a spur telephone line about one-third mile in length from the Crane Prairie line to the summit of Bates Butte, a small hill near the Big River Station which Mr. Oney uses for a secondary lookout point.

evidence.supports: First call over the line on July 7
evidence.quote: The first call over this line came in on July 7th.

evidence.supports: 1924 transfer of William Beaton to Paulina Peak from a temporary post on Bates Butte
evidence.quote: William Beaton had been transferred permanently to Paulina Peak from his temporary post on Bates Butte.

evidence.supports: August 1927 intermediate lookout due to extreme fire danger
evidence.quote: An intermediate lookout was stationed at Bates Butte due to extreme fire danger.

evidence.supports: Spur telephone line item dated July 21, 1915 (By July 1915 construction)

notes_for_editor: One source only: a directory entry that quotes three dated items (an item dated July 21, 1915 and attributed to The Deschutes Ranger, plus entries dated May 20, 1924 and August 5, 1927). The newspaper was not checked directly. No structure is described; the record's kind is unverified. A 2020s gravel-ride guide (dirtyfreehub.org) repeats the 1915 telephone-line claim without citing a source; it was not used. A search for a Bates Butte history, including one for 'Oney' and Big River, found no independent record. The cached NHLR and FFLOS Oregon indexes do not list Bates Butte. Deschutes NF archives may hold the originals.
